item.title: Architecting Governed, Self-Evolving AI Agents on Google Cloud
item.description: Learn how Project Chrysalis combines Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Agent Development Kit (ADK), BigQuery, and a four-gate defense-in-depth security stack (Model Armor, Cloud KMS, Binary Authorization, and OPA) to build governed, self-evolving AI agents that remediate live production outages in 1.8 seconds.

item.title: Streaming comes to API Gateway: real-time and AI-ready APIs, without changing your spec
item.description: API Gateway now supports real-time streaming—including Server-Sent Events, WebSockets, gRPC, and chunked transfer encoding—in Public Preview without requiring changes to your existing API specifications This update allows developers to route long-lived, bi-directional streams and AI workloads directly through the gateway while maintaining consistent authentication, rate limiting, and observability Additionally, gateways now feature deterministic default hostnames, simplifying environment provisioning and infrastructure-as-code management.

item.title: Single-tenant Titus: VM-level isolation on a multi-tenant container platform
item.description: This post is about them, and about single-tenant Titus, a mode that gives a task its own virtual machine while keeping everything else about Titus the same: the API, the deployment path, and the managed experience where the Compute/Platform team, not the application team, owns the host.We will walk through why shared-kernel isolation runs out of road for certain workloads, how we measure isolation rather than asserting it, the options we weighed (microVMs, gVisor, EC2, and more shared-kernel tuning) and why a dedicated VM inside Titus won, how the mode is built on the Titus federation layer and autoscaling, and what we have seen along three axes: isolation, fleet efficiency, and the operational cost of keeping the fleet patched.The cost of good neighborsMulti-tenancy is a tradeoff The job keeps the resources it requested; we recommend sizing it close to a node shape so the dedicated instance is well utilized, while keeping the workload portable and running identically whether in single-tenant mode or not, regardless of the host’s dimensions In aggregate, it can move the other way, for a reason related to how we dealt with poor isolation before single tenancy existed.To protect sensitive workloads on shared hosts, the platform used anti-affinity placement, scattering them across the fleet to reduce colocation of the same workload on the same nodes

item.title: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available
item.description: AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is a new security service that uses AI to automatically find, validate, and prioritize code vulnerabilities in your environment, then delivers ready-to-review fixes as pull requests replacing what previously took hours of manual investigation and days of cross-team coordination.

item.title: How bug bounty sharpens one researcher’s security skills
item.description: As Cybersecurity Awareness Month continues, the GitHub Bug Bounty team spotlights @r31n, diving into their research approach, favorite bug classes, and advice for aspiring hackers The post How bug bounty sharpens one researcher’s security skills appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

item.title: Trends from Money20/20 2026: The rise of “hidden” financial services
item.description: As fintech products become increasingly capable, the infrastructure behind them fades into the background Three trends from Money20/20 show how stablecoins, agents, and always-on money are changing financial services.
